distribution.name: OpenAI_math_research_catalog.csv
distribution.description:
This CSV contains metadata for mathematical research papers, including titles, abstracts, Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) codes, keywords, and links to each paper and its result family. Each row describes one paper and the result family it belongs to.

- Format: Comma-separated values (CSV)
- Encoding: UTF-8
- Delimiter: Comma (,)
- Quoting: Text fields that contain commas, such as description and `result_family_description`, are enclosed in double quotes.
- Shape: 722 rows, 12 columns
- Missing values: Represented as empty fields.
- Multi-valued fields: `msc_secondary` and `keywords` hold several values separated by semicolons. Split them before analysis.

**Data sample**

```csv
paper_name,description,main_subject,msc_primary,msc_primary_section,msc_secondary,result_family_number,result_family_title,result_family_description,keywords,paper_url,result_family_lean_url
An L³ bound for the trilinear Hilbert transform,"We prove that the trilinear Hilbert transform with fixed slopes 1, 2, 3 maps L³(ℝ) × L³(ℝ) × L³(ℝ) to L¹(ℝ), resolving this case of the trilinear Hilbert transform conjecture.",Real and complex analysis,42B20,Harmonic analysis on Euclidean spaces,42B25,86,An L³ bound for the trilinear Hilbert transform,"Proves that the principal-value trilinear Hilbert transform with shifts x-t, x-2t, x-3t is bounded from L³(ℝ)³ to L¹(ℝ). This resolves the L³ exponent case of the standard conjecture for slopes 1, 2, 3.",trilinear Hilbert transform; Hilbert transform conjecture; slopes,https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/preprints/An-L3-bound-for-the-trilinear-Hilbert-transform-October-5-2026/paper.pdf,
```

## Column schema

| Field | What (specific medium) | format-based comparison | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **paper_name** | Plain-text paper title | Free text, so titles can only be compared by exact string match | Free text, no controlled vocabulary |
| **description** | Free-text abstract-style summary | Prose cannot be compared across papers by format | Free text, no controlled vocabulary |
| **main_subject** | Short subject label, e.g., *"Number theory"* | Coarse grouping that allows comparison across subject areas | Controlled vocabulary of subject names |
| **msc_primary** | MSC 2020 code, e.g., *14C25* | Standardized codes allow precise cross-paper comparison | Controlled vocabulary ([MSC](https://msc2020.org/)): two digits, one uppercase letter, two digits |
| **msc_primary_section** | Top-level MSC section name, e.g., *"Algebraic geometry"* | Turns the primary code into a readable label for grouping | Controlled vocabulary matching official MSC section names |
| **msc_secondary** | Semicolon-separated MSC codes, e.g., *"14C30; 14K22"* | Multi-valued, so it must be split before comparison | Controlled vocabulary (MSC), separator "; " |
| **result_family_number** | Integer identifier, e.g., **1** | Groups papers that prove the same result | Integer, unique within the result-family list that ranges from 1 to 378 |
| **result_family_title** | Short title of the result family | Label for grouping across papers | Free text |
| **result_family_description** | Free-text summary of the shared result | Prose, so only useful for reading or NLP | Free text |
| **keywords** | Semicolon-separated terms | Uncontrolled terms (vary in spelling) | Uncontrolled |
| **paper_url** | URL to the PDF, hosted on GitHub | Circulation depends on the host | Must be an https URL, no controlled vocabulary |
| **result_family_lean_url** | URL to a Lean formalization | Only present where a formal proof exists | Optional |

name: OpenAI bulk release of mathematical papers dataset
description:
![](https://www.googleapis.com/download/storage/v1/b/kaggle-user-content/o/inbox%2F27942110%2Fccad270ae4099a3c947283293eb2e8fa%2Fgood-will-hunting.jpg?generation=1794404091736048&alt=media)
"Someone who opens up things for you. Touches your soul." *Good Will Hunting (1997)*. For centuries, the frontier of mathematics has been documented in the prose of academic and fundamentally human papers. The emergence of [formal verification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formal_proof) has introduced a new rigor: a proof is either logically perfect or computationally rejected. This gap between two worlds, the intuitive and the formal has long been the primary bottleneck in the quest for automated mathematical reasoning. This dataset is derived from the [OpenAI math catalog release](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenAI_bulk_release_of_mathematical_papers). For the researcher, this is more than a list of PDFs. Rather than treating mathematical papers as static documents, the dataset transforms them into a structured index. By pairing natural language descriptions with specific [Mathematics Subject Classification](https://msc2020.org/) (MSC) codes and "Result Families" the dataset enables the possibility to map the documents to each other. Data fetched from a collection of **721 machine generated papers** published during the OpenAI bulk release of early Autumn 2026: Main features: - **Paper Identity:** `paper_name` and `description` provide the title and the natural language summary of the mathematical findings. - **Classification:** `main_subject` categorizes the paper within the broader field of mathematics and is complemented with curated MSC columns. - **Logical Grouping:** `result_family_title` clusters related papers under a single unified mathematical result or conjecture. - **The Bridge:** `paper_url` (the original PDF) and `result_family_lean_url` (the formal code) provide the direct mapping between academic prose and Lean formalization. ## Related sources [OpenAI bulk release of mathematical papers](http://github.com/openai/math) ## License Licensed under the [CC0 license](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/).
